title: On Structural Explanation of Bias in Graph Neural Networks

problem.claim: GNNs can produce biased results against certain demographic subgroups, and the input network structure can influence this bias.

gap.claim: No studies had systematically identified which part of the input network structure leads to biased predictions for a given node, limiting transparency and safe adoption in decision-critical scenarios.

contributions.claim: The paper studies structural explanation of bias in GNNs.
The paper proposes a post-hoc explanation framework that identifies two edge sets: one accounting for exhibited bias and one contributing to the fairness level of a GNN prediction for a given node.
The proposed explanations are intended to support understanding of GNN prediction bias and fairness and the construction of effective, fair GNN models.

stated_novelty.claim: The authors characterize structural explanation of bias in GNNs as a novel research problem and describe their post-hoc explanation framework as novel.

author_reported_evidence.claim: Experiments on real-world datasets are reported to validate the framework's effectiveness in delivering structural explanations for GNN bias.
Open-source code is reported as available in the linked repository.

narrative_sequence.summary: GNNs perform well across graph analytical problems and are widely used in decision-making scenarios.
GNNs may be biased against demographic subgroups, with biased input structure identified as a significant source.
Prior work had not systematically determined which structural components cause biased predictions for individual nodes, limiting transparency and safe adoption.
The paper introduces a post-hoc framework that identifies edge sets associated with exhibited bias and prediction fairness.
The authors report practical significance, real-world dataset experiments, and an open-source implementation.

source_observation.claim: The framework identifies structural edge sets associated with bias and fairness for a given node.

interpretation.claim: Post-hoc structural attribution may make graph-model fairness behavior more inspectable at the node level.

application.claim: Use structural explanations to support fairness analysis and the design of fairer GNN models.

exception.claim: The abstract does not specify whether the explanations are reliable across graph domains, model architectures, or demographic settings.

unknowns: The abstract does not specify the explanation algorithm or optimization procedure.
The abstract does not identify the datasets, baselines, metrics, or quantitative results.
The abstract does not describe the two edge sets in formal detail.
